final_candidates.title: Handles - React Flow
final_candidates.product_feature: Distinct edge attachment handles and dynamic geometry refresh
final_candidates.version_or_date: Current next-site guide read 2026-11-24; exact version/date unknown.
final_candidates.exact_section: Using multiple handles; Dynamic handles; Hiding handles
final_candidates.input_processing_observation: Several incident edges -> select individually identified, positioned handles -> edges attach at separate positions on the same node.
final_candidates.what_is_new_vs_baseline: Adds explicit attachment identity and geometry refresh. Automatic count-based positioning is a proposed application policy, not a documented built-in feature.
final_candidates.changed_choice: If spacing means distinct endpoints, compute handle positions from the incident-edge count, preserve handle IDs, and refresh measured geometry after changes.
final_candidates.minimal_discriminating_input: Proposed T1: node A with two same-side source handles at one-third and two-thirds height, linked to B and C; compare against distinct IDs left at default positions, then add a third handle and recompute.
final_candidates.expected_output: Positioned handles produce separated endpoints; identifier changes alone can leave coincident positions. After recomputation and geometry refresh, endpoints should follow the new positions. Exact behavior remains unexecuted.
final_candidates.conditions_supported: Several edges on one node, with developer-controlled endpoint placement.
final_candidates.limitations: No native automatic-spacing algorithm demonstrated; per-count positioning is our inference. The source example uses different target nodes.
final_candidates.counter_evidence: Default handle centering and stale geometry can defeat spacing. The detailed hook link failed.
final_candidates.historical_availability: unknown: unpinned current page, not verified as available on 2024-01-01.

final_candidates.title: ParallelEdgeLayouter (yFiles-2.19 API)
final_candidates.product_feature: Grouped parallel-edge routing with adaptive distances and optional endpoint joining
final_candidates.version_or_date: yFiles Java 2.19 API; publication UTC unknown.
final_candidates.input_processing_observation: Edges sharing a node pair -> route one master path and derive peer paths -> automatically separated parallel segments.
final_candidates.what_is_new_vs_baseline: Adds a group-based routing stage and an explicit fixed-gap versus fit-to-node choice; absent from the input, not proven unknown to its author.
final_candidates.changed_choice: If spacing means parallel paths between the same pair, group peer edges and decide whether node attachment or a fixed gap governs tight cases.
final_candidates.minimal_discriminating_input: Proposed T2: two horizontally aligned nodes only eight units high, three peer edges, requested gap twenty; compare adaptive spacing against fixed spacing with unjoined ends.
final_candidates.expected_output: Adaptive routing should keep attachments on node bounds by allowing a smaller gap. Fixed spacing with unjoined ends can miss node bounds. Test geometry and exact paths remain unverified.
final_candidates.conditions_supported: Multiple edges between the same pair, suitable master path, optional shared endpoints.
final_candidates.limitations: Narrower than arbitrary fan-out; Java API requires an adapter or independent implementation for React Flow.
final_candidates.counter_evidence: The requested gap may shrink under adaptation; joined endpoint segments cease to be parallel.
final_candidates.historical_availability: unknown: API is labeled 2.19 with copyright through 2025; neither verifies availability at the request date.

final_candidates.title: Routing multiple edges between two nodes in a parallel fashion
final_candidates.version_or_date: Applies to Java editions 2.5–2.18; publication UTC unknown.
final_candidates.input_processing_observation: Create an edge or move one endpoint -> collect the affected peer group and reroute it -> spacing updates without rerouting unrelated edges.
final_candidates.what_is_new_vs_baseline: Provides concrete update triggers and affected-group selection, beyond a static spacing configuration. It uses the same router as candidate 2.
final_candidates.changed_choice: Recompute all peers when group membership changes, and scope movement updates to affected connections.
final_candidates.minimal_discriminating_input: Proposed T3: A–B has two edges, including a reverse edge; C–D has one bent edge. Add a third A–B edge and compare rerouting only the new edge with rerouting the peer group.
final_candidates.expected_output: The demo reroutes all A–B peers while leaving C–D out of that routing pass. Expected visible spacing and preserved unrelated geometry are unexecuted predictions from the code.
final_candidates.conditions_supported: Automatic updates after edge creation and one-endpoint movement.
final_candidates.limitations: Java-specific; same mechanism as candidate 2. Movement is an optional discriminator, not a newly imposed requirement.
final_candidates.counter_evidence: No deletion update is shown, and edges whose two endpoints move together are excluded from movement rerouting.
final_candidates.historical_availability: unknown: version range and site copyright do not establish this article's publication or availability in January 2024.
